artists.biography:
Simple Minds are a Scottish rock band who achieved worldwide popularity from the mid-1980s to the early 1990s. 
The band produced a number of critically acclaimed albums in the early 1980s and best known for their No. 1 US, Canada and Netherlands hit single "Don't You (Forget About Me)", from the soundtrack of the John Hughes film The Breakfast Club. They are also known for the No. 3 US hit single "Alive and Kicking" and the No. 1 UK hit single "Belfast Child". The band has sold more than 60 million albums since 1979. 
The core of the band is the two remaining founder members - Jim Kerr (vocals, songwriting) and Charlie Burchill (guitars, keyboards after 1990, other instruments, songwriting) - and drummer Mel Gaynor (who first joined the band in 1982). The other current band members are Andy Gillespie (keyboards) and Ged Grimes (bass guitar). Significant former members include bass guitarist Derek Forbes and keyboard player Michael MacNeil (the latter credited as a significant band composer during the band's rise in the 1980s).

perplexity.description:
Street Fighting Years," released in 1989, is the eighth studio album by Simple Minds, produced by Trevor Horn and Stephen Lipson. The album marks a stylistic shift from the band's earlier rock anthems toward a more reflective, layered sound with political and social themes. It incorporates orchestral arrangements and traditional instruments such as bagpipes and bodhran, contributing to its rich, atmospheric texture. The album includes the UK No.1 single "Belfast Child," a reworking of a traditional folk song, and features songs inspired by political figures and events, such as the title track written in memory of Victor Jara.

In the context of Simple Minds' discography, "Street Fighting Years" represents a mature, contemplative phase following their mid-1980s rock successes like "Once Upon a Time" and "Sparkle in the Rain." It was their fourth UK number-one album, reflecting both commercial success and critical recognition. The album's political engagement and musical depth distinguished it from previous releases, earning it a lasting reputation among fans and critics. Although some later reissues included additional material of mixed reception, the original 1989 release remains a significant work in the band's career.
